statement: Every color pair listed in tokens/checks/contrast.pairs.json meets its WCAG 2.2 AA ratio in every brand and mode, unless the brand opts out with a stated reason.

check.test: [contrast-aa-tokens] contrast: a text role set too close to its surface fails, naming brand, mode, both roles and both ratios, and writes nothing

statement: On a rendered Artifact page at 375 and 1280 wide, in light and dark, text meets 4.5:1, or 3:1 when large (24px and up, or 18.66px and up at weight 700 and up); disabled text, SVG text, and text on gradients, images or unknown backgrounds are skipped.
The token target.hit-target-min is at least 44px in every brand and mode; this does not show that any component uses it.

check.test: [hit-target-token] systemGate: hit target: a value under 44 fails the build, naming the token, and writes nothing

statement: Opt-in: a CSS rule marked /* orrery-control */ sets no pixel width or height under 44px, unless it is also marked /* orrery-hit-area: pseudo */; unmarked rules are not checked.

check.test: [hit-target-source] source rules: control-min-size fails a marked control under 44px, naming the property and selector, and passes an unmarked rule, a 44px control and a pseudo hit area

statement: Every rendered interactive element has a hit area of at least 44px on each axis.

reason.text: Checkable on Artifact pages in the Artifact checker's rendered pass; not built in this lane. For kit components the real floor is the rendered hit-area test in the Phase 2 component specs.

statement: The accent role, which is the focus ring's color, meets 3:1 on page, layer-1 and layer-2 in every brand and mode, unless the brand opts out with a stated reason; this does not show that a component draws the ring.

check.test: [focus-ring-contrast] focus ring: an accent too close to the page fails, naming the ring role, the surface and both ratios, and writes nothing

statement: On an Artifact page, each focus ring found by tabbing through up to 40 stops meets 3:1 against the surface around it; an element with no ring only warns.
Every focusable element shows a visible focus ring.

reason.text: Checkable in the Artifact checker's rendered pass, which already finds the no-outline case but only warns (artifact/check/check.mjs, 'no visible focus outline'); making it fail is not built in this lane. A source scan cannot know which elements are focusable.

statement: Every spring in tokens/base/motion.tokens.json declares $reduced as opacity, none or instant.

check.test: [reduced-motion-form] reducedMotionGate: reduced motion: a spring with no $reduced fails the build, naming the spring, and writes nothing

statement: A component honors the reduced-motion form its motion role declares.

reason.text: Whether a component swaps its spring for the declared form is behavior; it needs a rendered component under prefers-reduced-motion, which the Phase 2 component tests can assert.

statement: A scrolling region does not sit inside another scrolling region.

reason.text: Checkable in the Artifact checker's rendered pass (computed overflow of each ancestor); not built in this lane. artifact/check has no such rule today.

statement: Nothing sits above a title or heading only to categorize, date or restate it.

reason.text: Whether a line is a kicker depends on its role beside a heading; artifact/SKILL.md states the rule but artifact/check has no rule for it.

statement: CSS, JS, TS and HTML files given to the source checker contain no em dash (character, entity or escape) outside comments.

check.test: [no-em-dashes] source rules: em-dash fails an em dash, its entity and its escapes, naming file, line and rule, and passes a comment and clean text

statement: Status is written as a word, never carried by color or an icon alone.

reason.text: Whether an element carries a status with no word is a judgement about its meaning; artifact/check bans status hue (token-colors) and icons (no-emoji-icons) but cannot see a status that has no word.

statement: On an Artifact page checked with --brand, a rendered color that equals the brand accent or on-accent and equals no other token appears only as an .os-button fill or ink.
The accent color appears only on the primary button fill and the focus ring.

reason.text: token-colors runs the accent test only with --brand, allows any .os-button rather than the primary one, never verifies the ring, and skips a value equal to a locked token (artifact/check/core.js:276-286); proving this needs a rendered pass that knows which button is primary.

statement: In CSS files given to the source checker, a color is a var(); a hex, color function, named color or system color appears only as a var() fallback, or on a declaration excused by an orrery-allow marker with a reason.

check.test: [no-literal-color] source rules: literal-color fails a bare hex, color function, named color and system color, naming file, line and property, and passes a var() fallback

statement: In CSS files given to the source checker, a px value that a space or radius token already holds is written as that token, including negative values and custom properties whose name contains pad, gap, margin, space, inset or radius; other custom properties and declarations excused by an orrery-allow marker with a reason are skipped.

check.test: [no-literal-spacing] source rules: literal-spacing fails a pixel value a space or radius token holds, naming the token to use, and passes a var() and an off-scale value

statement: In JSX and TSX files given to the source checker, an object literal in a style, animate, initial, exit, whileHover or whileTap attribute (directly, or as a ternary or && branch) holds no literal color and no spacing or radius value a token already holds; style={identifier}, values built in code, transform and translate offsets, and TS outside those attributes are not read.

check.test: [inline-style-literal] source rules: inline-style-literal fails a literal color and a token-sized spacing number in style={{ }}, and passes var() values and off-scale numbers

statement: No gradients or decorative color inside the package.

reason.text: A held decision, not a technical limit: the source scanner could detect gradient functions, but DESIGN.md:85 conflicts with the trigger highlight DESIGN.md:110 describes, so the wording needs Sean's call before any check is added.

statement: Every role in tokens/base/roles.tokens.json is set by each brand and mode, or opted out of with a stated reason.

check.test: [required-roles] source: required roles: a role missing from one mode fails, naming brand, mode and role

statement: A brand sets only the token paths its lock list unlocks.

check.test: [brand-lock] locks: lock list: a brand that inherits the default list and sets a locked path fails, naming brand and path

statement: An opt-out names a known check, pair or role and gives a reason.

check.test: [opt-out-reasons] readOptOuts: opt-out: one with no reason fails, naming the brand and the opt-out

statement: Every file in tokens/generated/ equals a fresh build of the token source.

check.test: [generated-matches-source] driftGate: drift: a generated file that differs, is missing or is stale fails, naming the file

statement: A srgb color's hex equals its components.

check.test: [hex-matches-components] colorGate: color gate: hex and components that disagree fail, naming the token

statement: The generated Artifact contract equals artifact/snapshot/tokens.json.

check.test: [artifact-contract-matches] snapshotGate: snapshot gate: a changed snapshot value fails, naming the key

statement: The generated CSS declares the same tokens as artifact/head.py, for no brand and for each client brand.

check.test: [head-py-matches] cssGate: head.py gate alone: generated CSS that drifts from head.py fails while the snapshot gate passes

statement: Each promoted spring equals its constant in src/motion.ts.
Every --orrery-iris-* variable the package CSS reads is written by the package or documented in README.md, and every documented one is read.

check.test: [css-var-audit] audit: a variable the CSS reads that nothing writes or documents fails the audit

statement: Every variable in the opt-in Iris bridge is documented in README.md, maps to a role that exists, and that role's brand-orrery light value equals Iris's literal fallback in src/styles.module.css; it does not show how Iris looks in dark.

check.test: [iris-bridge-matches-fallbacks] irisBridgeGate: a role whose light value no longer equals the Iris literal fails the build, naming both values, and writes nothing
